key_insight: LungAI improved malignancy risk assessment for screening-detected lung nodules and, when integrated with Lung-RADS v2022, reduced cancers assigned to 12-month surveillance and benign biopsy referrals.
clinical_relevance: This imaging AI study—not a drug-discovery study—suggests potential to refine screening triage, with reported reductions of 46% in cancers assigned to the slowest surveillance pathway and 20% in benign biopsy referrals.
method: Validated a deep-learning nodule malignancy classifier on a held-out NLST test cohort.
Compared discrimination with Sybil, nodule diameter, estimated volume, and Lung-RADS v2022.
Applied prespecified score cutpoints to reclassify cases within existing Lung-RADS management pathways.
evidence_signal: Across 2,747 CT examinations from 1,244 patients, including 89 cancers, LungAI achieved AUROC 0.92 and AUPRC 0.47; versus weighted Lung-RADS assessments, AUPRC improved significantly but AUROC did not.
watch_item: LungAI is investigational and not FDA-cleared; triage estimates relied on a weighted, cancer-enriched annotated subset rather than prospective implementation outcomes.
paper_title: LungAI: An AI Biomarker that Refines Lung-RADS v2022 Triage of Screen-Detected Pulmonary Nodules
